# Advisor terminal: talk the escalation through with the real agent in a terminal on the run page

## What to build

On the escalation screen, **Talk to an agent** starts an **advisor**: the run provider's **interactive** CLI (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `qwen`) in a PTY, in its own worktree at the integration head. Its first message is `Read <runDir>/escalations/<id>/advisor.md and follow it.`

That context file holds:
- the escalation and the other open ones;
- the spec path;
- the tasks with their status;
- the escalated branch and its base;
- the resolution schema with an example;
- the rules: talk it through, don't change the repository, write the agreed resolution to `<runDir>/escalations/<id>/draft.json`, and run `<node> <cli> resolve --run <run-id> --file <draft>` when the user asks to apply it.

The terminal shows on the screen with the shared xterm client, through a WebSocket route on the run page server. Reloading the page reattaches with the scrollback, and **Restart** starts a new session. The draft then appears in the existing draft summary (with **Apply resolution**). When the agent applies the resolution itself, the screen closes on `escalation:resolved`. The advisor is killed and its worktree removed when the escalation is resolved or the run ends.

The fake provider gets an `interactive()` that runs a small line-based fake advisor, so all of this is testable without a model. When `node-pty` can't be loaded (sandboxed runs), the screen says `The advisor terminal isn't available here (node-pty is missing). Write the draft by hand or use graph-execution resolve.`

All engine paths are relative to `packages/graph-execution/`. Spec: `docs/prd/escalation.md`, sections "Advisor", "HTTP routes", "Run page" and "Fake provider".

## Context: files to read before implementing

**What earlier tasks built (in the codebase now):**
- Shared terminal module, `src/terminal/`:
  - `createPtySession({ file, args, cwd, env, cols, rows })`, which lazily imports node-pty and has a scrollback ring;
  - `bridgeSocket(socket, session)` with the protocol: client `{type:"input"|"resize"|"ping"}`; server `{type:"replay"|"data"|"exit"|"restart"|"pong"}`;
  - the browser client `src/terminal/client.ts` → `mountTerminal(host, { url, Terminal, FitAddon, WebglAddon?, PredictiveEchoAddon?, theme?, onConnection?, onExit?, ... })`, copied by the postbuild into `dist/web/assets/terminal/`.
  - The engine depends on `ws`, `@xterm/xterm`, `@xterm/addon-fit`, `@xterm/addon-webgl` and `xterm-zerolag-input`.
- Escalation screen (`src/web/assets/escalation.js`):
  - `mountEscalation`, with a placeholder `<div id="advisor-<id>" class="advisor">`;
  - the draft summary refreshed from `GET /escalations/<id>/draft` and the `drafts` counter in the `/state` snapshot;
  - `src/escalation/draft.ts` (`draftPath`, `readDraft`, `watchDrafts`).
- `graph-execution resolve [--run <id>] --file <f>` (`src/launch/resolve.ts`). It posts to the live run (using `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_TOKEN` when set) or applies offline.
- The resolution format `resolutionSchema` (`src/escalation/resolve.ts`), `loadEscalations` / `openEscalations` (`src/escalation/store.ts`), and the events `escalation:open` / `escalation:resolved`.
- graph-manager's run proxy passes WebSockets through.

**Files to read:**
- `src/providers/types.ts`: `AgentRole` at line 1 (add `"advisor"`); `Provider` at 38-41.
- `src/providers/claude.ts`, `codex.ts`, `opencode.ts`, `qwen.ts`. The one-shot args builders (`claudeArgs` 30-35, …) pass the prompt on stdin with the `GRAPH_EXECUTION_<NAME>_ARGS` extras.
- Interactive command lines used by graph-manager's agent buttons (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.ts` 94-135): `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` (with `--standalone` for OpenCode 2+, via `cliMajor`), `qwen`. The installed `claude --help` shows `claude [options] [command] [prompt]`, which starts an interactive session with a first message. For codex, opencode and qwen, check `<bin> --help` for how to pass a first message. If a CLI has no such argument, write the first message into the PTY as input after start, followed by `\r`.
- Provider wrappers that build `Provider` objects and must forward `interactive`:
  - `teeOutput` (`src/runner/run.ts` 931-946);
  - `watchLoops` (`src/agents/loop.ts` ~91);
  - `watchIdle` (`src/agents/idle.ts` ~16);
  - `trackProcesses` (`src/state/processes.ts` ~96).
  Test literals that build `Provider` objects without it must still compile, so make `interactive` **optional** on the interface.
- `src/providers/fake.ts`: `run` 195-219; `fakeScriptSchema` at 53 (loose entries; add `draft: z.unknown().optional()`).
- `src/providers/spawn.ts`: `RUN_ENV_UNSET` (`src/state/paths.ts` 25-37) unsets `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUNS_ROOT`, the WEB_* variables and others for agents.
  - The advisor PTY env must **keep** `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUNS_ROOT` and `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_TOKEN`, so its `resolve` command finds the run and authenticates.
  - Set `GRAPH_EXECUTION_HANDOFF=detached` and `SSH_CONNECTION=1`, as graph-manager's terminals do, so the CLI never tries to open a browser.
- CLI path: `fileURLToPath(new URL("../cli.js", import.meta.url))` with an injectable override, as in `src/launch/launch.ts:64`, plus `process.execPath` for node. Under vitest this points at `src/cli.js`; tests use the built `dist/cli.js` (`src/__fixtures__/suite.ts:11-12`).
- `src/agents/summarizer.ts` 31-153 (the pattern for an agent module with its own work dir, label and files).
- `src/runner/references.ts` (the spec and task copies under `<runDir>/context/`).
- `src/git/git.ts:51`: `addWorktree --detach` (detached worktree at a ref); `removeWorktreeIfPresent`.
- `src/web/server.ts`: the Host, token and Origin checks at 525-532; `http.createServer` at 584-589; `closeServer` at 596-603.
- `src/web/page.html` and `src/web/assets/escalation.js`.
- `src/web/assets.ts` 7-10 (asset content types).

## Patterns to follow

**Upgrade checks.** An upgrade is a GET, so the existing Origin check skips it. Repeat the checks by hand in `server.on("upgrade", (req, socket, head) => …)`:
- `Host` must be in `hosts`, else write `HTTP/1.1 421 Misdirected Request\r\n\r\n` and destroy;
- the token must match when set, else 401;
- `Origin`, when present, must be `http://<one of hosts>`, else 403.
Then use `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true }).handleUpgrade(req, socket, head, (ws) => bridgeSocket(ws, session))`.

**Relative WebSocket URL in the page:**
```js
const u = new URL(`escalations/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/advisor/terminal`, location.href);
u.protocol = u.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:";
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE providers

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `Provider.interactive?(o: { cwd: string; firstMessage: string; model?: string }): { file: string; args: string[]; env?: Record<string, string>; typeFirstMessage?: boolean }`;
  - claude: `{ file: CLAUDE_BIN, args: [...(model ? ["--model", model] : []), firstMessage] }`;
  - codex: `codex [--model m] <message>` (check `codex --help`);
  - opencode: `opencode` (plus `--standalone` when `cliMajor("opencode") >= 2`; copy the version check from `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agents.ts` 67-96 into the engine provider), with `typeFirstMessage: true` unless its help shows a prompt option;
  - qwen: per `qwen --help` (`-i <prompt>` if it exists, otherwise `typeFirstMessage`);
  - every wrapper forwards `interactive`.
- **VALIDATE**: unit tests for each command line (the provider test files use `writeFakeBin`; argv-only tests need no binary).

### CREATE `src/providers/fake-advisor.ts` and the fake `interactive()`

- **IMPLEMENT** a node program (compiled to `dist/providers/fake-advisor.js`), started as `process.execPath fake-advisor.js <contextFile> <scriptFile?> <id>`:
  1. Print `advisor ready (<id>)\r\n`.
  2. Read stdin lines (the PTY sends `\r`; split on `\r` or `\n`). For each line print `you said: <line>\r\n`.
  3. On `draft`: write the script's `advisor:<id>` entry's `draft` (from `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT`) to the draft path read from the context file (a line `Draft file: <path>`), then print `draft written`.
  4. On `apply`: run the resolve command from the context file (a line `Apply command: <cmd>`, with the command in a JSON array to avoid quoting issues) and print its output.
  5. On `exit`: exit 0.
- The fake provider's `interactive()` returns `{ file: process.execPath, args: [<dist path of fake-advisor.js>, …] }`. Compute the dist path from `import.meta.url` with a fallback to `../../dist/providers/fake-advisor.js` when running from `src` under vitest.
- **VALIDATE**: a unit test that spawns it with plain pipes (not a PTY) and checks `draft` and `exit`.

### CREATE `src/agents/advisor.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `advisorContext(input)` writes `<runDir>/escalations/<id>/advisor.md` with these sections:
    - `# Escalation <id>`: reason, evidence, questions;
    - `## Other open escalations`;
    - `## Spec` (its path in `<runDir>/context/spec/`);
    - `## Tasks`: id, status and the first line of each task's content, plus the path of the full task files (`<runDir>/tasks/` or the context copy);
    - `## The escalated work`: `git diff <baseSha>..<branch>` (the command to run, not its output);
    - `## Resolution format`: the zod shape written out, plus one `continue` example and one `change` example;
    - `## Rules`: as listed above, plus `Draft file: <path>` and `Apply command: ["<node>","<cli>","resolve","--run","<id>","--file","<draft>"]`, and a human-readable version of the command.
  - `class AdvisorSessions`:
    - `start(id)` creates the detached worktree `<runDir>/worktrees/advisor-<id>` at the integration head (`addWorktree --detach`, `src/git/git.ts:51`), writes the context, and calls `createPtySession` with the provider's `interactive()` command. When `typeFirstMessage` is set it writes the first message plus `\r` to the session after spawn;
    - `get(id)`, `restart(id)`, `stop(id)`;
    - `stopAll()` removes the worktrees.
    - A missing `interactive` gives the error `the <provider> provider has no interactive mode`. A node-pty import failure gives the "isn't available here" message above.
  - Emit `escalation:advisor` `{ id, status: "running" | "exited" }` (add it to `RunEventMap`).

### UPDATE `src/runner/run.ts` and `src/web/start.ts` / `server.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - The run creates `AdvisorSessions` when escalation is on. It stops the session for each id on `escalation:resolved`, and calls `stopAll()` in `execute`'s `finally`. It passes the sessions object into the UI options (`advisors`) and from there to `createWebServer`.
  - Routes:
    - `POST /escalations/<id>/advisor` → start if not running, `200 { running: true }`;
    - `POST /escalations/<id>/advisor/restart`;
    - `404` for an unknown id; `409 { error: { code: "not_open" } }` for a resolved one; `501 { error: { code: "unavailable", message } }` when the advisor can't run.
  - The upgrade handler for `/escalations/<id>/advisor/terminal`, with the checks above, then `bridgeSocket`. It closes with `4404` when there is no session.
  - `closeServer` closes WebSocket clients.
  - `snapshot()` adds `advisors: Record<id, "running" | "exited">`.

### UPDATE the page

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - **Vendoring.** In the postbuild, copy the browser builds of `@xterm/xterm` (JS + `css/xterm.css`), `@xterm/addon-fit`, `@xterm/addon-webgl` and `xterm-zerolag-input` from `node_modules` into `dist/web/assets/vendor/xterm/`. Inspect the packages' `lib/` folders first:
    - if ES module builds exist (`.mjs`), load them with `import()` from relative URLs and add `.mjs` to `assets.ts`'s content types;
    - otherwise load the UMD builds with `<script>` tags created on demand, and read the globals.
    Document the choice in `src/web/assets/vendor/README.md`. Resolve the packages with `createRequire` from the engine folder in a small `scripts/vendor-xterm.mjs` called by the postbuild.
  - **Screen.** In `escalation.js`, the advisor area gets a **Talk to an agent** button:
    1. It posts `escalations/<id>/advisor`, loads the vendored classes, and calls `mountTerminal(div, { url, Terminal, FitAddon, WebglAddon, PredictiveEchoAddon, instantEcho: true })` from `assets/terminal/client.js`.
    2. Once started, the button becomes **Restart**.
    3. An `unavailable` answer shows its message.
    4. When the page reloads while `advisors[id] === "running"`, it mounts the terminal at once (the replay restores the output).
    5. Link `assets/vendor/xterm/xterm.css` in `page.html`.
  - The tab closes on `escalation:resolved` (already true), so the agent applying the draft itself also closes it.

### Tests

- **IMPLEMENT** `src/web/web-advisor.test.ts` (`skipIf(win32)` if node-pty is flaky there; CI also runs Windows):
  1. An in-process run with the fake provider and the script `{ "task:2": { attempts: [{ escalate: {…} }] }, "advisor:E1": { attempts: [], draft: { escalationIds: ["E1"], action: "continue", guidance: "B" } } }`. Set `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT` to a file with that script, because the fake advisor is a separate process.
  2. `POST escalations/E1/advisor` → 200.
  3. Connect with `ws` to `escalations/E1/advisor/terminal`: the first message is `replay` and it contains `advisor ready (E1)`.
  4. Send `{type:"input",data:"draft\r"}`. Poll `GET escalations/E1/draft` until the draft is there.
  5. Send `apply\r`. The run resolves E1 through the CLI (use the built `dist/cli.js`) and finishes with exit 0. `escalation:resolved` is seen, and the advisor session is stopped.
  6. Upgrade checks: a foreign Origin → 403, a missing token (with `listen.token` set) → 401, an unknown id → closed with 4404.
  Also add a unit test for `advisorContext` (the sections and the apply command).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/web/web-advisor.test.ts src/agents/advisor.test.ts src/providers`

### Look at it (required by TESTING.md)

- **IMPLEMENT**: build, then start a fake `--web` run where task 2 escalates and `advisor:E1` has a draft.
  1. In agent-browser: open the Decision tab, click **Talk to an agent** and take a screenshot. Check that the terminal shows `advisor ready (E1)` with the right size and theme.
  2. Type `draft`: the draft summary appears.
  3. Reload: the terminal reattaches with its output.
  4. Type `apply`: the tab closes and the run finishes.
  5. Repeat through graph-manager if it is available in your environment: open the run from graph-manager and check that the terminal connects through its proxy.
  Add a section "Escalation" to `TESTING.md` with the commands to see the escalation screen and the advisor terminal with the fake provider (the scripts above).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Talk to an agent** starts the provider's interactive CLI in `<runDir>/worktrees/advisor-<id>` with the first message pointing at `advisor.md`. The terminal shows on the page.
- [ ] `advisor.md` contains the escalation, the other open escalations, the spec and tasks paths, the diff command, the resolution format with examples, the draft path and the apply command.
- [ ] Reloading the page reattaches with the scrollback; **Restart** starts a new session.
- [ ] A draft written by the agent appears in the summary, and **Apply resolution** works. The agent running the apply command resolves the escalation, and the tab closes.
- [ ] The advisor is stopped and its worktree removed when the escalation is resolved and when the run ends.
- [ ] The WebSocket enforces Host, token and Origin; an unknown id closes with 4404.
- [ ] Without node-pty, the screen shows the "isn't available here" message and the rest of the screen works.
- [ ] The fake provider's interactive advisor makes the whole flow testable. `TESTING.md` has the "Escalation" section.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- src/web src/agents src/providers src/escalation
npm test
```
